newsitem.title: JAPAN: IHI to invest 10 bln yen for aircraft parts plant.
newsitem.headline: IHI to invest 10 bln yen for aircraft parts plant.

text.p: Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd (IHI) said on Friday it would invest 10 billion yen to build a new plant in Japan to produce aircraft engine parts to meet increasing demand from the civil aircraft manufacturing industry.
Construction of the plant in Fukushima prefecture, north of Tokyo, will begin in October, and the plant is due to start operating in the autumn of 1998, an IHI spokesman said.
The heavy machinery maker said it would make turbines and other jet engine parts but would not disclose its planned production volume.

"Rising demand can be attributed to a need to replace old aircraft, a shift in the appropriate size of aircraft in certain routes, and an increase in the number of people who travel," the IHI spokesman said.

IHI said the new plant would handle orders for engine parts it received from General Electric Co and Rolls-Royce Plc as part of a joint production agreement with other companies. IHI would not reveal details of the orders.
IHI said it expects to increase production of V2500 engines for small aircraft to an annual 300 units by the year ending March 31, 1999, compared with 100 units in 1996/97.
The company also said it hopes to raise production of engines for medium-sized airplanes to 180 units from 90 units during the same period.
